statements.text: When the vector tables have another width, schema init is refused. It says to run again with the rewidth flag.
statements.notes: Cypher HTTP server on AUDITE (vector columns at the width PyOps reports, empty) and `ivg --url ... schema init --embedding-dim <width+3>`: the server's initialize_schema raised EmbeddingIdentityConflict before writing (_refuse_width_change is read-only), the server answered 409, the CLI printed 'Schema init refused (409)' and 'run it again with --rewidth', exit 1; no net change in AUDITE (table ID counters allowed, none changed); width unchanged after.
live_cases: ivg schema init --embedding-dim 7 (tables at 4) -> 409, exit 1, names --rewidth

statements.text: With no IRIS address given, a direct command is refused and names the settings to set.
statements.notes: `ivg embeddings inventory` and `ivg fhir status rx17g` with IRIS_HOST unset (child env): exit 1, stderr 'No IRIS connection: set IRIS_HOST (and IRIS_PORT / IRIS_NAMESPACE / IRIS_PASSWORD) or pass --iris-host.'; 0 journal records. The ivg script ran the pin's worktree package (observation).
live_cases: ivg embeddings inventory with no IRIS_HOST -> exit 1 naming IRIS_HOST/--iris-host
ivg fhir status with no IRIS_HOST -> exit 1 naming IRIS_HOST/--iris-host

statements.text: On a namespace that refuses the engine, most calls are refused. Setup, status, legacy removal and close still run.
statements.notes: Engine with schema_prefix RX17ALT on AUDITE (records Graph_KG): construction answers, then create_node, get_node, node_count, execute_cypher and the store's get_nodes raise IVGSchemaError at entry, 0 journal records (the refusal holds); status() and remove_legacy_objects(dry_run=True) run (EXEMPT_METHODS, schema_name.py:376-377). The close clause does not hold: IRISGraphEngine has no close method (EXEMPT_METHODS names one the engine lacks), and the store's close() (a no-op, iris_sql_store.py:4278-4279) is guarded without exemptions (engine.py:390) and raises IVGSchemaError. Setup (initialize_schema) was not run on the refused engine: on a mismatched record it would refuse (refuse_other_record) and a failure of that check would deploy a second schema into the shared namespace; exemption inspected (schema_name.py:376-377). New finding F-C1715 (S4).
live_cases: engine on schema RX17ALT: construction answers (the check is pending)
refused engine: its store's close() still runs
refused engine: its store's get_nodes is refused

statements.text: A name that cannot name a graph is refused before IRIS is asked.
statements.notes: engine.verify_graph('0'), ('a\x01b'), (42): ValueError from validate_graph_name, the method's first statement (before the Native API call at :888); 0 journal records.

statements.text: A failed listing raises. It does not answer an empty list.
statements.notes: list_active_queries has no handler: any failure propagates. Live: an engine's connection closed under it -> ProgrammingError (<COMMUNICATION LINK ERROR>) raised, not []; control on an open connection answered rows. A failed SQL listing (the unit test's case) is not producible here without a refused statement; the closed connection exercises the same no-handler path.
live_cases: list_active_queries on a connection that fails -> raises, not []

statements.text: When IRIS refuses to end the process, kill query logs a warning and returns false.
statements.notes: kill_query('999999999') and kill_query('not-a-process'): returned False with a logged warning, not raised; 0 journal records. Observation: IRIS answers the statement with SQLCODE -359 ('User defined SQL function %SYSTEM.SYS.KILLPROCESS does not exist'), so every call takes this branch: kill_query on the lane's own scratch process (pid 140416, killable) also answered False and the process was still alive. The refusal holds as stated; kill_query cannot end any process here (new finding F-C1716, outside the refusal).
live_cases: kill_query('999999999') -> False with a warning, not raised
kill_query('not-a-process') -> False with a warning, not raised

statements.text: A real removal is refused in a caller transaction that holds a write. Nothing is done.
statements.notes: START TRANSACTION + INSERT ($TLEVEL 1): remove_legacy_objects(dry_run=False) -> CallerTransactionOpenError, 0 journal records, $TLEVEL still 1, the caller's row still pending; dry_run=True in the same transaction answered a list (allowed, as stated).
live_cases: remove_legacy_objects(dry_run=False) with a caller write -> CallerTransactionOpenError
remove_legacy_objects(dry_run=True) in the same transaction is allowed

statements.text: The host layer refuses any call to a system method whose name starts with a percent sign.
statements.notes: host_for(connection) (ClientHost): call('Graph.KG.Snapshot','%New'), call_large(same), call('Graph.KG.Meta','%ExistsId','1') -> HostError naming the method, before _call; 0 journal records. InProcessHost shares Host.call/call_large (host.py:151-156); it needs embedded IRIS and was not built here.

statements.text: In a program outside IRIS, an in-IRIS connection is refused. The error names the network connect call.
statements.notes: Child Python (not irispython; the iris-embedded-python-wrapper answers with MagicMocks): IRISGraphEngine(EmbeddedConnection()) and EmbeddedConnection().cursor().execute('SELECT 1') each raise EmbeddedUnavailableError (an ImportError) whose message names iris.connect(host, port, namespace, user, password). The cursor object itself is created lazily; the refusal comes at its first use (as the upstream test test_a_cursor_says_so_too checks).
live_cases: EmbeddedConnection outside IRIS: engine and cursor refused naming iris.connect

statements.text: When the strict setting is on, a namespace mismatch is an error.
statements.notes: IVG_STRICT_NAMESPACE=1, IRISGraphStore(AUDITE connection, namespace='USER'), first class-method call: no exception (it answered AUDITE); a NamespaceMismatchWarning is issued (warnings.warn, :837-838), not raised. Existing finding F-1703, reproduced again.
live_cases: IVG_STRICT_NAMESPACE=1, store namespace='USER' on an AUDITE connection -> error

statements.text: If the class list cannot be read for want of a right, the engine raises. It does not take that as no classes.
statements.notes: _detect_capabilities re-raises ClassesUnreadable instead of answering 'not deployed'. Evidence: upstream unit tests (a refused dictionary read, ClassesUnreadable) passed here in val-unit-3-c02. Not triggered live: it needs a login refused read on the routines database/class dictionary (a second IRIS user/role: container security configuration, not available to this lane).

statements.text: Any other failure undoes the whole write and raises a write error.
statements.notes: IRISGraphStore.write_nodes([rx17:w1, rx17:<300 x>]): the second INSERT fails (SQLCODE -104, node_id over 256), txn.rollback(), GraphWriteError('store.write_nodes', 'nothing written'); rx17:w1 absent after. Journal net change only in the table ID counters and ^KG("__version"), which the nodes write advances with $Increment outside the transaction (a rollback does not take a counter back; noted as allowed patterns, not content).
live_cases: store.write_nodes: second node id over 256 chars -> GraphWriteError, first undone

statements.notes: IRISGraphStore.execute_transaction([INSERT rx17:t1, INSERT into a missing table]): SQLCODE -30 on the second, rollback, GraphWriteError; rx17:t1 absent; journal net change only in table ID counters.

statements.text: Deleting a node that still has edges is refused, unless the query detaches them.
statements.notes: engine.execute_cypher("MATCH (n {node_id: 'rx17:d1'}) DELETE n") with an edge rx17:d1-R->rx17:d2: GraphWriteError 'ConstraintVerificationFailed: Cannot delete node with existing relationships. Use DETACH DELETE.' after the rollback; node and edge still there; journal net change only in counters. Control: DETACH DELETE removed it.
live_cases: Cypher DELETE of a node with an edge -> refused (ConstraintVerificationFailed)

statements.text: A refused key or a forbidden request raises a client error with the status code.
statements.notes: Server with IVG_API_KEY, client with a wrong key: execute_cypher (query), stats and schema (reads) -> IVGClientError http_code 401 (hold); explain (a query, POST /admin/explain) and load_ndjson -> httpx.HTTPStatusError, not IVGClientError (they call raise_for_status without _refused, sdk.py:166-182). Read-only server (IVG_READ_ONLY=true): a CREATE via execute_cypher -> IVGClientError 403 (holds); load_ndjson -> HTTPStatusError 403. Existing finding F-1714 (reproduced again; the async client was not re-probed).
live_cases: read-only server: CREATE via execute_cypher -> IVGClientError 403
